FOREWORD
This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Drinks and Carbonated Beverages Sectional Committee had been approved by the Food and Agriculture Division Council.
Non-alcoholic beverage bases (concentrates) are used in the preparation of f>Yrup and then beverages at homes by adding the same to a fixed-volume solution of sugar in potable water with or without carbonation. For the purpose of preparing the sugar solunon, a fixed amount of sugar is added to a particular volume of water, as declared by the manufacturer.
]0

the preparat ion of this standard. due consideration has been given to the Prevention of Food Adul,eJv'an (fFA), ACI, 1954 and the Rules framed thereunder. This standard is SUbject to the i estricnons rrnj-ose d under these Rules, wherever applicable.

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requn-ement of this standard IS complied with, the final value, observed OJ' calculated, expressing the result of a lest or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 'Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised Y. The number of significant places retained In the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in thrs standard.

The use of the Standard Mark 15 governed by the provtsicns of the Bureau 0/ Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulatrons made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of tha t standard under a well defined system of inspectron, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by HIS and operated by the pTO~ ducer , Standard marked products are also continuously checked by HIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of condttrcns under which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtamed fr om the Bureau of Indian Standards.
